title: Choosing Arrays, Strings and Vectors
learningObjectives: Compare built-in arrays, std::array, std::string and vector.
Select fixed-size or resizable storage appropriately.
Choose text-specific or numeric collection types.
Evaluate safety, interface clarity and size requirements.
Justify a collection choice for a concrete task.

understand.concept: Raw arrays, std::array, std::string and std::vector differ in fixed/dynamic size, text semantics and interfaces.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing a container makes code safer and clearer.
understand.explain: Prefer standard containers; choose based on fixed size, dynamic size, or text.

practise.guidedTask: For Choosing Arrays, Strings and Vectors, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on Choosing Arrays, Strings and Vectors: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.
